market_view: South African shares fell 6.9% and the rand weakened 4.4% to about R17.49/$ as October CPI jumped to 5.2%, the Reserve Bank held the repo rate at 7.25% in a 4-3 vote calling it only a pause, and Gauteng coalition talks unsettled investors. In New York the S&P 500 dropped 8.6% into a correction and the Nasdaq 10%, led by a rout in AI chip and memory stocks such as Nvidia, Micron and Sandisk, while futures still price a Fed hike on 9 December. Gold fell 9.5%, platinum 13.4%, copper 9.8% and Brent 6.1%, with iron ore near four-year lows, so investors should expect continued volatility in miners and rate-sensitive shares and keep some cash and quality, dollar-earning businesses until inflation and rate signals settle.
